result.topic_en: Section 12 of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift draft on trigonometric series: it remarks that the representability conditions could be weakened slightly, then turns to completing Dirichlet's treatment of functions without infinitely many maxima and minima, including functions that become infinite at finitely many points.

items.english: Dirichlet's proof leaves in fact nothing to be desired on two points. First, in the integral expressions for the nth term of the series and for the sum of its first n terms, the contribution of all intervals ultimately becomes infinitely small as n grows. The exceptions are the intervals where the function becomes infinite and those infinitely close to the argument value of the series. Second, the integral converges to pi f(x+0) for infinite n when 0<b<pi and f(t) does not become infinite between the limits.
